q: Per Sec. 5, the Construction Manager may take what form(s)?
o: Only a licensed corporation
Only a partnership of architects and engineers
An individual or a firm
Only a sole proprietorship owned by the Owner
n: Sec. 5 states plainly that the Construction Manager may be an individual or a firm. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 5)

q: Sec. 2.1 states that the CM's responsibilities include the functions of which group?
o: The Board of Architecture
The Construction Supervision Group (CSG)
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
The Project Feasibility Team
n: Sec. 2.1 states that the CM's responsibilities include the functions of the Construction Supervision Group (CSG), referencing Doc. 204-A and the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 2.1)

q: What does the acronym IAPOA, referenced in Sec. 5.1 of SPP 204-B, stand for?
o: Institute of Architects and Planners of Asia
International Alliance of Professional Organizations of Architects
Integrated Association of Philippine Owners and Architects
Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects
n: IAPOA stands for the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects, of which the RLA acting as CM must be a member in good standing. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 5.1)

q: An Owner has already directly hired a Construction Supervision Group (CSG) for a project and separately engages an Architect as CM. Per Sec. 2.2, what is the CM's relationship to that CSG?
o: The CM may supervise the CSG hired directly by the Owner
The CM must absorb the CSG's functions into his own personal duties
The CM must terminate the CSG and hire a new one under his own employ
The CM has no authority over the CSG in this case
n: Sec. 2.2 provides that the CM may hire the CSG to be under his employ, or may instead supervise a CSG that was hired directly by the Owner. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 2.2)

q: Per Sec. 6.1, how are Construction Management services compensated?
o: As part of the Architect's basic design fee, with no additional charge
Through a fixed government-mandated flat rate regardless of project size
Separately, since construction management is not part of the Architect's regular services
Only through profit-sharing with the Contractor
n: Sec. 6.1 states that since construction management is not part of the regular services of the Architect, the services rendered by the Architect as CM shall be separately compensated. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 6.1)

q: While acting as CM, an Architect personally directs a subcontractor's crew on-site in a manner that a court could interpret as the Architect assuming the Contractor's own liability for the work. Which provision does this risk violating, and which Civil Code article is referenced?
o: Sec. 5.1; Article 1723 of the Civil Code
Sec. 3.1; Article 1723 of the Civil Code
Sec. 3.2; Article 1900 of the Civil Code
Sec. 4.1; Article 1159 of the Civil Code
n: Sec. 3.1 prohibits the CM from involving himself directly with the Contractor's work such that it may be construed that he is assuming the Contractor's liability, citing Article 1723, etc. of the Civil Code. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 3.1)

q: Which earlier document did the 2010 SPP Document 204-B replace?
o: 2000 SPP Document 204
1979 UAP Doc. 204-A
1979 UAP Doc. 205
1979 UAP Doc. 204-B
n: The heading of SPP Document 204-B explicitly states it is "replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 204-B." (Source: SPP Document 204-B, heading)

q: Per Sec. 4.1, to whom is the Architect acting as CM directly responsible, and for what aspects of the work?
o: The Owner; for programming, coordination, quality and cost control, and time management
The Contractor; for site safety only
The Building Official; for code compliance only
IAPOA; for professional discipline matters
n: Sec. 4.1 states the Architect as CM is directly responsible to the Owner on all aspects of the construction work: programming, coordination, quality and cost control, and time management. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 4.1)

q: Per Sec. 1.2, which of the following correctly lists ALL the capacities in which a Construction Manager (CM) may serve?
o: A government-accredited engineer, a subcontractor, or the project's structural engineer
Only a firm hired by the Contractor
A member of the Owner's staff or a government housing official, but never an independent individual
A member of the staff of the Owner, an independent individual, or a firm hired by the Owner
n: Sec. 1.2 lists three capacities: a member of the staff of the Owner, an independent individual, or a firm hired by the Owner to manage construction of a particular project. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 1.2.1-1.2.3)

q: Equipment fails to function due to a deficiency in the manner of construction (not the design). Under Sec. 4.2.2, when is the CM free of liability?
o: Only if the Contractor admits fault in writing
Only if the failure occurs within the first month of construction
Provided the CM faithfully discharged his function/s during the construction/project implementation
The CM is always liable, since the manner of construction is his direct responsibility
n: Sec. 4.2.2 states the CM assumes no liability for equipment failure or collapse due to deficiencies in the manner of construction, provided the CM faithfully discharged his function/s during the construction/project implementation. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 4.2.2)

q: Per Sec. 1.3, what qualifies an Architect to serve as Construction Manager?
o: His training in various specialties, which allows him to supervise and assure proper coordination of construction activities with regard to quality, workmanship and cost
Completion of a mandatory CM certification course under IAPOA
At least ten years of continuous employment with a single Contractor
A separate CM license issued by the Professional Regulation Commission
n: Sec. 1.3 states that the Architect's training in various specialties allows him to serve as CM and supervise and assure proper coordination of all construction activities with regard to quality, workmanship and cost. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 1.3)

q: Per Sec. 5.1, what must the individual CM (or the principal of a firm CM) be, apart from being a State-regulated professional?
o: Preferably an Architect with managerial capabilities and extensive construction experience, a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA) with an updated professional identification card, and a member in good standing of IAPOA
A civil engineer holding a valid contractor's license
Any professional regardless of field, provided he is bonded by insurance
A graduate of a construction management degree program, with no licensure requirement
n: Sec. 5.1 requires the individual/principal to preferably be an Architect with managerial capabilities and extensive experience in construction, a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA) with an updated professional identification card, and a member in good standing of IAPOA. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 5.1)

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four functions listed in Sec. 2.1.1-2.1.4 as part of the CM's responsibilities?
o: Coordination and Supervision
Keeping of Records
Quality Control of Work
Preparation of the detailed architectural design
n: The four listed CM/CSG functions are Coordination and Supervision, Cost and Time Control, Quality Control of Work, and Keeping of Records. Preparing the detailed architectural design is a regular design service, not a CM function. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 2.1.1-2.1.4)

q: Per Sec. 5.2, which architects are described as "usually capable of becoming Construction Managers"?
o: Only architects who have never worked with a Contractor
Architects who are Contractors or who have already been in responsible charge of construction works
Only fresh graduates newly licensed by the PRC
Only architects employed exclusively by government agencies
n: Sec. 5.2 states that Architects who are Contractors, or who have already been in responsible charge of construction works, are usually capable of becoming CMs. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 5.2)

q: Per Sec. 3, the Architect acting as CM is limited from doing which of the following?
o: Involving himself directly with the Contractor's work in a way construed as assuming the Contractor's liability, and imposing methods, systems or designs that substantially affect the construction schedule and impair the design concept
Receiving separate compensation for CM services
Coordinating construction activities with the Owner
Keeping records of cost and time control
n: Sec. 3.1 and 3.2 set the two limitations on the CM's authority: not assuming the Contractor's liability, and not imposing methods/systems/designs that substantially affect the schedule and impair the design concept. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 3.1-3.2)

q: SPP Document 204-B primarily covers which subject, and under what legal framework does it operate?
o: Project feasibility studies; part of the IRR of R.A. No. 545
Construction Supervision Group services; a standalone SPP not tied to any law
Construction Management Services; part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266
Design-build services; part of the National Building Code
n: SPP Document 204-B covers Construction Management Services and forms part of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of R.A. No. 9266, the Architecture Act of the Philippines. (Source: SPP Document 204-B, title/heading)

q: As CM, an Architect unilaterally imposes a new construction method that substantially changes the schedule and alters his own original design concept. Under Sec. 3.2, is this within his authority as CM?
o: No, but only if the Owner had not pre-approved the original design
Yes, because the CM has full authority over all means and methods
Yes, provided the Owner is not informed of the change
No — Sec. 3.2 prohibits imposing methods, systems or designs that substantially affect the construction schedule and impair the design concept
n: Sec. 3.2 explicitly limits the CM from imposing methods, systems, or designs that will substantially affect the construction schedule and impair the design concept of the Architect. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 3.2)

q: According to Sec. 1.1, what industry condition led to the institution of Construction Management Services?
o: A legal mandate that all projects above a certain cost use a Construction Manager
A nationwide shortage of licensed architects available to supervise construction
The phase-out of the Construction Supervision Group system
Increasing complexity of construction projects, creating demand for more effective cost control and faster project implementation without sacrificing quality
n: Sec. 1.1 states that due to the increasing complexity of construction projects, there is an upward demand for more effective cost control and faster project implementation consistent with high quality of work, which Construction Management Services were instituted to address. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 1.1)

q: A portion of a building collapses due to a deficiency in the plan/design. Under Sec. 4.2.1, when is the CM NOT liable for this?
o: Provided the CM did not participate in the plan/design review and approval
In all cases, regardless of the CM's involvement in design review
Only if the CM is also the original design architect
Never — the CM is always liable for design deficiencies
n: Sec. 4.2.1 provides that the CM assumes no liability for collapse due to deficiencies in the plan/design, provided the CM did not participate in the plan/design review and approval. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 4.2.1)

q: An Owner wants to engage a CM but insists the person already be a salaried member of the Owner's own organization rather than an outside hire. Is this arrangement allowed under SPP 204-B?
o: No, the CM must always be an independent third party
No, the CM must always be a firm, never an individual staff member
Yes — Sec. 1.2.1 explicitly allows the CM to be a member of the staff of the Owner
Yes, but only if that staff member is also the project's Contractor
n: One of the three recognized capacities for a CM under Sec. 1.2.1 is being a member of the staff of the Owner, so this arrangement is permitted. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 1.2.1)
